metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overreact; reduce forecast peak magnitude by 5–15%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true mean.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.5) within 3–5 days of forecast, model should adjust downward by 3–8% per day of negative sentiment.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >+10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 2–5% per day until convergence.
- When true outcome shows early sharp decline (e.g., 3–5 days of -5%+ drop), model often misses it; add 1–3 day lag correction to downward trend.
- Forecast should not exceed 10% above or below 14-day moving average unless driven by strong sentiment or event context.
